story.title: The Eating-Joint
paragraphs_en: Rohan’s father owned a small eating-joint on the national highway. Many vehicles used to stop by the joint and passengers used to savour a healthy snack or a small meal. Many tasty items were prepared including chole-bhatture, Indian thalis and a variety of curries. Many type of sweets like gulab jamun and halwa were made too. Rohan loved the food. Often he used to rush back to the joint after school to consume a tasty meal on a charpai under the banyan trees. Rohan was a brilliant student and when he passed school, he got admission in a reputed college. He used to come home only during the holidays. Once his education was over, he came home and wanted to start his own business. His father had grown old and wanted him to take over the responsibilities of running the joint.

Rohan was not ready for this, but he still accompanied his father to the joint. The joint was the same as the one he had left years ago. “It is so expensive to run this joint. Our profits are at an all time low. If the expenses keep rising, I will have to close this joint that I built with so much effort” Rohan’s father said unhappily. “Don’t worry, daddy. I will help you find a solution to this problem. I will find out where exactly the problem lies,” Rohan reassured his father. He started looking around the joint. The vegetables, fruits and spices were bought at low prices from a nearby town. Their customers paid them well. “I wonder, then, how does it become so expensive to run the joint - when our monthly costs are under control - why is our monthly bill so high?” thought Rohan.

The next day Rohan was enjoying piping hot aloo parathas. He felt thirsty and ordered some water. He drank a glass of water. He was still thirsty, so he ordered another glass. When the second glass came, he drank just half the glass and his thirst was quenched. He threw the leftover water away in the sink. As soon as he threw it in the sink, he realized something. It was the wastage of water that made running their small joint so expensive! He noticed that almost all customers did not empty their glasses. The water was mostly wasted. Their workers washed the utensils under running tap water, this led to further water wastage. The joint was also cleaned using water from pipes rather than water stored in buckets. They were using more water than needed everywhere! They had to buy more water at more expensive prices. All this made the functioning of the joint costly and difficult. Moreover, so many litres of water that were being wasted could be used for better purposes. Rohan decided to do something about this.

He made colourful posters urging his customers to order only as much water as they would actually use. He personally spoke to his customers to prevent water wastage. He installed a huge pit and requested his customers and employees to throw the leftover drinking water in it. A pipe was connected to this pit. This pipe discharged water into a garden in the backyard. The plants grew taller and stronger in the garden and were laden with beautiful blossoms. He asked his staff to store water in buckets and use them for chores like cleaning and washing. He also minimized the water used in cooking by rationing the amount of water that would be enough for each day. This made cooking quicker and the operating of the food joint more efficient. Soon, the news of this type of water management spread far and wide.

Rohan was interviewed by prominent magazines, and later that year, their joint won the Most Eco-Friendly Organisation of the Year Award. This made their joint very famous and more people started visiting it. Rohan had realized that it was important to conserve its resources for the organization to be successful. He took over his dad’s eating joint and also opened a small business of his own where he educated different restaurants on how to save resources like water to be successful.
